caption: A foot block never turns its ranks further off its heading when it straightens up after riders have been inside it. A brittle cavalry troop charges a 48-man infantry block standing on Hold. The block first snaps round toward the riders, turning its men in place so its ranks stand about 66 degrees off the way it faces. Then the riders ride into its ranks, and as the men turn to face them where they stand, the block's heading swings back and on past its ranks, about 22 degrees beyond them. Once the riders have broken and gone, the block turns its ranks back by those 22 degrees and stops square. Undoing every turn it made toward the riders, as it did before this fix, would wheel its ranks on round to about 66 degrees off its heading with no order given.
